requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then created with UID/GID 1000, home /home/appworker, and /bin/bash. Its existence and attributes were directly confirmed again after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to limits of 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: The persistent limits configuration specifies nofile=8192 and nproc=256. Actual appworker login sessions directly reported matching soft and hard limits both before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral verification. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities: node1 changed from fbdf5b2c-bb43-49f6-935d-fb98f8a972f6 to 17c59d29-3ece-4940-9378-0deff187325c and recovered cleanly.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands had clear roles: creating the required account, installing its limits configuration, or performing the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary mutations were identified. The restart was acknowledged, changed the boot identity, and recovered a running system with the account, configuration, effective limits, expected sockets, package health, and no failed services. The transient connection timeout is consistent with the reboot and caused no mutation or hygiene concern.
